question: In what year were the first modern Olympic Games held?
explanation: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in April 1896, organized largely through the efforts of Pierre de Coubertin, who revived the ancient Greek Olympic tradition. The games featured 241 athletes from 14 nations competing in 43 events, with Greece winning the most medals at home.

question: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cups?
explanation: Brazil has won the FIFA World Cup five times (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002), more than any other nation. Brazil is also the only country to have qualified for every single FIFA World Cup since the tournament began in 1930. Germany and Italy have each won four titles, and Argentina has won three.

question: What is the maximum score in a single frame of bowling?
explanation: The maximum score in a single frame of bowling is 30 points, achieved by bowling a strike in the frame itself plus two more strikes in the bonus balls (i.e., getting three consecutive strikes starting with that frame). In the 10th (final) frame, a bowler can roll up to three balls, and three strikes equals 30 points for that frame.

question: In tennis, what is the term for winning a game without the opponent scoring a point?
explanation: In tennis, winning a set 6–0 (shutting out the opponent in an entire set) is called a 'bagel,' because the zero resembles a bagel's round shape. The term 'breadstick' is used informally for winning 6–1, and 'double bagel' for winning a match 6–0, 6–0. An 'ace' is a serve the opponent cannot return.

question: Which swimmer has won the most Olympic gold medals?
explanation: Michael Phelps won 23 Olympic gold medals (and 28 total medals) across the 2000, 2004, 2008, 2012, and 2016 Olympics, making him the most decorated Olympian in history. He famously won 8 gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Olympics alone, surpassing Mark Spitz's record of 7 gold medals at a single Olympics (set in 1972).

question: What is the name of the trophy awarded to the winner of the NHL playoffs?
explanation: The Stanley Cup is awarded to the champion of the NHL playoffs and is the oldest professional sports trophy in North America, donated by Canadian Governor General Lord Stanley of Preston in 1892. The Presidents' Trophy goes to the team with the best regular-season record, and the Conn Smythe Trophy is awarded to the playoff MVP, not the championship team.

question: In cricket, what is a duck?
explanation: In cricket, a 'duck' is when a batsman is dismissed without scoring any runs (a score of zero). The term supposedly comes from 'duck's egg,' which refers to the oval shape of a zero. A 'golden duck' is being dismissed for a duck on the very first ball faced, and a 'diamond duck' is being run out without facing any balls.

question: Which country invented the sport of rugby union?
explanation: Rugby union is said to have originated at Rugby School in Rugby, Warwickshire, England, when in 1823 a pupil named William Webb Ellis supposedly picked up the ball during a game of football and ran with it. The sport was codified and formalized in England, and the Rugby World Cup trophy is named the Webb Ellis Cup in his honor.

question: How many players are on a basketball court per team during a game?
explanation: Each team fields 5 players on the court at a time in regulation basketball (NBA, FIBA, NCAA), meaning 10 players total are on the court during play. Teams typically have rosters of 12–15 players, with substitutions allowed during dead balls. The five positions are traditionally point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward, and center.

question: What year did Muhammad Ali defeat Sonny Liston to win his first world heavyweight title?
explanation: Muhammad Ali (then known as Cassius Clay) defeated Sonny Liston on February 25, 1964, in Miami Beach, Florida, to win the world heavyweight championship when Liston failed to answer the bell for the seventh round. The upset was one of boxing's greatest shocks, as Liston was a massive favorite; Ali announced his conversion to Islam and name change the following day.

question: In baseball, how many outs are needed to end a half-inning?
explanation: Three outs are required to end a half-inning (one team's turn at bat) in baseball. Since a full inning consists of both teams batting, each team must record three outs before they switch from fielding to batting. This structure has been fundamental to baseball since its formalization in the 19th century.

question: Which country won the inaugural Rugby World Cup in 1987?
explanation: New Zealand's All Blacks won the inaugural Rugby World Cup in 1987, held jointly in Australia and New Zealand, defeating France 29–9 in the final in Auckland. The All Blacks are historically the most successful team in international rugby, and their winning of the first World Cup cemented their place at the pinnacle of the sport.

question: What is the distance of a marathon in miles?
explanation: A marathon is 26.2 miles (42.195 kilometers), a distance standardized at the 1908 London Olympics when the course was set at exactly 26 miles and 385 yards to run from Windsor Castle to the Olympic stadium finish line in front of the royal box. The distance was later officially adopted by the International Amateur Athletic Federation in 1921.

question: In golf, what term is used for two strokes under par on a hole?
explanation: An eagle is the term for completing a hole in two strokes under par — for example, scoring a 3 on a par-5 hole. A birdie is one under par, an albatross (or double eagle) is three under par, and a bogey is one over par. The bird-related terminology is thought to originate from American slang in the 19th century where 'bird' meant something excellent.

question: Which Formula 1 driver has the most World Championship titles?
explanation: Lewis Hamilton holds the record for the most Formula 1 World Championship titles with seven, tied with Michael Schumacher's previous record and then surpassed (both have seven). Hamilton won his seventh title in 2020, and has also set records for most pole positions, most wins, and most podiums in F1 history.

question: What sport is played at Wimbledon?
explanation: Wimbledon in southwest London hosts The Championships, Wimbledon, the oldest and most prestigious tennis Grand Slam tournament in the world, held annually since 1877. It is played on grass courts, making it the only remaining Grand Slam played on grass; the other three Slams are played on hard courts (Australian and US Opens) and clay (French Open).

question: How long is an Olympic swimming pool in meters?
explanation: An Olympic-size swimming pool is 50 meters long, 25 meters wide, and at least 2 meters deep, with 8–10 lanes each 2.5 meters wide. This is called a 'long course' pool; many pools used for training and lower-level competitions are 25-meter 'short course' pools, and world records are kept separately for both pool lengths.

question: In soccer/football, what does VAR stand for?
explanation: VAR stands for Video Assistant Referee, a technology-based system introduced by FIFA in which a team of officials reviews footage of match incidents (goals, penalty decisions, direct red cards, and mistaken identity) to assist the on-field referee in making more accurate decisions. It was first used at the 2018 FIFA World Cup in Russia.

question: Which NBA team has won the most championships?
explanation: The Boston Celtics have won the most NBA championships with 18 titles (through the 2024 season, when they won their 18th), surpassing the Los Angeles Lakers (17 titles). The Celtics dominated the NBA in the late 1950s and 1960s under coach Red Auerbach and players like Bill Russell, winning eight consecutive titles from 1959 to 1966.

question: Which country has won the most Cricket World Cup titles?
explanation: Australia has won the most Cricket World Cup titles with six wins (1987, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2015, and 2023), making them the most successful team in World Cup history. West Indies won the first two World Cups (1975 and 1979), India has won twice (1983 and 2011), and England won their first title in 2019.
